why_it_matters: Statins work by blocking a pathway the body also uses to make coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), and some research has found lower CoQ10 levels in people taking statins long-term.
talk_to_pharmacist_if: you experience muscle aches, weakness, or unusual fatigue while taking a statin

why_it_matters: Diuretics increase how much potassium and magnesium the kidneys remove from the body, which can lead to low levels with ongoing use.
supplements_to_discuss: Ask your pharmacist whether a potassium or magnesium supplement is appropriate for your specific diuretic
talk_to_pharmacist_if: you experience muscle cramps, weakness, or an irregular heartbeat while taking a diuretic
clinical_source: General pharmacology literature on diuretic-associated electrolyte depletion — sample content for demo; pharmacist must supply a verified citation before real use

nutrient_concern: Magnesium, Calcium, and Vitamin B12 concerns
why_it_matters: Long-term use of PPIs can reduce how well the body absorbs magnesium, calcium, and vitamin B12, since stomach acid plays a role in absorbing each of these.
foods_that_may_help: eggs, dairy, fish, and fortified cereals (vitamin B12)
supplements_to_discuss: Ask your pharmacist whether a magnesium, calcium, or B12 supplement is appropriate, especially if you've taken a PPI for longer than a year
talk_to_pharmacist_if: you've taken a PPI for longer than a year, or experience muscle cramps, an irregular heartbeat, tingling, or unusual fatigue
clinical_source: FDA Drug Safety Communication (March 2011) on PPI-associated low magnesium — sample content for demo; pharmacist should confirm current citation and add calcium/B12-specific references

nutrient_concern: Reduced overall nutrient intake — protein, Vitamin B12, iron, Vitamin D, and thiamine — due to appetite suppression and delayed gastric emptying
why_it_matters: GLP-1 medicines can significantly reduce appetite and slow digestion, which sometimes makes it harder to get enough protein and key vitamins and minerals from food alone.
foods_that_may_help: protein-rich, easy-to-tolerate foods (eggs, Greek yogurt, lean meats, fish, protein shakes)
vitamin B12 sources (eggs, dairy, fish, fortified cereals)
supplements_to_discuss: Ask your pharmacist about a protein supplement or a multivitamin, especially if you're eating noticeably less than before
talk_to_pharmacist_if: you notice unusual weakness, numbness, tingling, vision changes, or have trouble keeping up your food and fluid intake
clinical_source: Retrospective cohort literature on GLP-1RA-associated nutritional deficiencies (2025–2026 observational studies) — sample content for demo; pharmacist must supply a verified citation before real use
